security_audit.summary: All 66 static findings are false positives caused by documentation language about CCXT exchange APIs, order workflows, HTTP behavior, and identifiers. Manual review of SKILL.md found no prompt injection or executable payload. The skill is documentation-only, but users should protect exchange credentials and validate any live-trading implementation.

remediation.issue: The skill includes examples and guidance for order submission.
remediation.suggestion: Add a prominent safety note that live orders require explicit user confirmation, parameter validation, and a non-production test path.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance may involve verbose exchange logs.
remediation.suggestion: State clearly that API keys, secrets, signatures, and authenticated request data must be redacted before sharing logs.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md begins with text before YAML frontmatter.
remediation.suggestion: Move the translated-content label below valid YAML frontmatter so automated metadata parsers can scan the file reliably.

content.value_statement: Exchange APIs differ in symbols, order rules, and capabilities, which makes trading integrations difficult to implement correctly. This skill helps you use CCXT documentation to build, inspect, and troubleshoot those integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explain CCXT unified methods for markets, tickers, balances, orders, and trades.
Help compare exchange capabilities and identify supported methods.
Guide market-buy, reduce-only, stop-loss, and take-profit order workflows.
Explain rate limits, asynchronous requests, and common API errors.
Help prepare concise CCXT issue reports without exposing API credentials.
limitations: It provides documentation guidance and does not execute trades or access exchange accounts.
Exchange support and parameters can change after the bundled documentation was created.
It cannot guarantee order execution, prices, liquidity, or exchange availability.
It is not financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

use_cases.title: Prototype an exchange connector
use_cases.description: Plan a CCXT integration that loads markets, validates symbols, and retrieves public market data.

use_cases.title: Review an order workflow
use_cases.description: Check market-buy cost handling and reduce-only parameters before adding an order flow to an application.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot an API error
use_cases.description: Interpret a CCXT error and prepare a minimal, credential-free reproduction for support or debugging.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: fetch market data
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to use CCXT to load markets and fetch a ticker for one symbol. Include the checks I should make before using the result.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: compare capabilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to inspect whether my CCXT exchange supports a requested order feature. Explain what to do when it is unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: design guarded order handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a CCXT order workflow with symbol validation, amount and price precision checks, rate limiting, dry-run logging, and explicit user confirmation before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: investigate a failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose this CCXT error. Ask for a minimal credential-free example, library version, exchange name, method, full error, and sanitized verbose request and response.

output_examples.input: How can I avoid sending the wrong amount in a spot market buy?
output: Explain whether the exchange expects base amount or quote cost.
Recommend checking the market-buy capability and price requirement.
Suggest validating precision and using a non-production test path first.

output_examples.input: Why does my CCXT request fail after several calls?
output: Identify rate limiting as a likely cause.
Recommend enabling CCXT rate limiting and reducing concurrent requests.
Request the exchange name, method, sanitized error, and library version.

best_practices: Use read-only market-data calls before enabling any account or trading feature.
Keep API credentials outside prompts, source control, logs, and verbose support reports.
Validate exchange capabilities, symbols, precision, and order costs before submitting an order.
anti_patterns: Do not place live orders from unreviewed examples or assumptions about exchange parameters.
Do not disable rate limiting to overcome request failures.
Do not share API keys, secrets, or unredacted authenticated request data when debugging.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It provides CCXT documentation guidance and does not access an exchange account or execute trades.

faq.question: Which languages does CCXT support?
faq.answer: The bundled documentation covers JavaScript, Python, and PHP usage.

faq.question: Can it tell me whether an exchange supports a feature?
faq.answer: It can explain how to inspect CCXT capabilities and exchange metadata for a feature.

faq.question: Should I provide my API key for debugging?
faq.answer: No. Remove API keys, secrets, signatures, and other sensitive values before sharing logs or examples.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a trade will succeed?
faq.answer: No. Order acceptance depends on the exchange, account permissions, market conditions, and current API behavior.

faq.question: Is this investment advice?
faq.answer: No. The skill explains software integration and does not provide investment, legal, tax, or financial advice.
